expectations.text: Has a generic table formatter function (print_table or equivalent)
expectations.evidence: print_table(tasks: &[Task]) is Task-specific (hardcoded 5 columns, fixed HEADERS array). Not a generic table formatter — it only accepts &[Task].

expectations.text: Routes to JSON when --json is set, table otherwise (dual-mode output)
expectations.evidence: print_tasks(tasks, format: OutputFormat) matches on Table vs Json and dispatches to print_table or print_json accordingly. list.rs converts the json bool flag to OutputFormat.

expectations.text: Has a hint/next-steps function that prints suggestions to stderr
expectations.evidence: No hint function exists anywhere in the output files. There is no stderr hint/suggestion mechanism.

expectations.text: Table output is borderless (no +, |, or --- border characters)
expectations.evidence: output.rs line 67-68: `let sep: Vec<String> = widths.iter().map(|&w| "-".repeat(w)).collect(); write_row(...)` — prints a dashed separator line between header and data rows.

expectations.text: Formats due_date for human readability (not raw ISO/Debug)
expectations.evidence: format_row uses `dt.format("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M").to_string()` — a human-readable date format, not raw ISO or Debug output.

expectations.text: Has a type-specific renderer function for Tasks (not generic JSON dump)
expectations.evidence: print_table is Task-specific with custom columns (ID, TITLE, STATUS, DUE, PRIORITY) and format_row does Task-specific formatting (short ID, date formatting).
